name: Kingdom of England

areaKm2.note: The world_1000 England polygon measures 112,547 km2 on the sphere (low); modern England is ~130,000 km2 and the 1066 kingdom held all of it bar Cumbria (mid).

population.note: Darby: the 268,984 Domesday households (1086) indicate 1.2-1.6 million; the Economy of England article gives ~1.5 million in 1086; higher estimates up to ~2.25 million allow for omitted landless and subtenants (Postan). 1066 was probably slightly higher than 1086 (harrying of the North 1069-70).

urbanization.note: About 5.5% of the population lived in urban areas in 1086.

activePersonnel.note: Standing element: royal and earls' housecarls ("as many as 3,000" by the late 11th century; Cnut kept 3,000-4,000) plus royal thegns in attendance.

trainedReserves.note: Select fyrd: "England could furnish about 14,000 men" (one man per five hides). Harold's army at Hastings is put at 5,000-13,000, most agreeing on 7,000-8,000 (Norman Conquest article); Norman chroniclers' 400,000 and 1,200,000 are rejected. Per the feudal-host convention the fyrd is reserve, not standing force.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Butsecarls and crews of royal ships, household officials.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. The great fyrd of all free men for local defence on top of the select fyrd.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Housecarls and thegns fighting dismounted in a shield wall with Dane axe, spear and sword (Housecarl article: up to 3,000 royal housecarls).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: mail byrnie, helm, kite shield, Dane axe; but no cavalry arm.

count.note: Educated guess. A few archers in royal service; English archery was weak at Hastings.
Educated guess. Longships of the ship-fyrd (one ship per 300 hides); Harold kept a fleet off the Isle of Wight all summer 1066 until it dispersed on 8 September. Crews come with the levy.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Harold proven in Wales (1063) and at Stamford Bridge; forced marches but committed at Hastings without waiting for reinforcements.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: household troops loyal to Harold; the northern earls Edwin and Morcar held back.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: defending the homeland, victorious at Stamford Bridge (25 Sept).

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: Dane axe, spear, sword, few bows; no crossbow, no cavalry lance.

armor.note: Anchor 3 (mail): byrnie and conical helm for the elite.

fortification.note: Anchor 2-3: burhs with earth-and-timber walls, Roman city walls; almost no castles.

logistics.note: Anchor 3: Roman roads, royal estates (feorm) feeding the army.

communications.note: Anchor 2-3: riders and the shire system.

isr.note: Anchor 2-3: coastal watch, but the Norman landing at Pevensey went unopposed.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (via OWID): United Kingdom 1000 = 1,151 (2011 int$). England was the richest part of the British Isles, so mid near that value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Heregeld abolished in 1051; service in kind from the five-hide unit.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Textiles, metalwork, minting (~50,000 pounds of coin in circulation before 1066, Economy of England article).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Open-field agriculture feeding ~5.5% urban population.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Usable Roman roads (Watling Street, Ermine Street, Fosse Way) and herepaths.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. London, Sandwich, Dover, Southampton, Bristol, York, Chester.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. North Sea and Channel trade.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Domesday records plough teams of eight oxen across tens of thousands of manors, plus horses; ~0.3 animals per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar terrain, local supply, burhs and broad population support; island position.

notes: Snapshot = September 1066, Harold II between the Norwegian landing and Stamford Bridge (25 Sept) and before Hastings (14 Oct). The shares above follow the feudal-host convention: activePersonnel = housecarls and thegns in royal service; the select fyrd (~14,000) is trainedReserves. Modern estimates of Harold's army at Hastings run 5,000-13,000 (most 7,000-8,000), William's 7,000-12,000 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Conquest). Population convention: the kingdom south of the Tweed-Solway line excluding Wales and Cumbria.
